target_customer: Tech platforms and marketplaces such as Outdoorsy, Deel and Guesty that want to sell insurance to their users
problem: Platforms want to embed insurance but face underwriting, insurer access and compliance work they are not set up to do.
business_model: B2B API and software plus insurance program access, with revenue from platform fees and insurance economics

founders.name: Matheus Riolfi
education: University of Sao Paulo and Kedge Business School, dual business degree
founders.background_notes: Licensed insurance broker per YC page.

founders.name: Jerome Selles
education: ENSTA ParisTech, MSc in Applied Mathematics
founders.background_notes: Met Riolfi at Turo while working on its international insurance program (Digital Insurance, 2022-02-25).

competitors.name: Cover Genius
competitors.what: XCover embedded insurance distribution platform for e-commerce, travel and marketplaces
competitors.traction_then: Tripled gross written premium and signed 20 new partners in the prior six months (as reported Sept 2021); partners included Amazon, eBay, Wayfair, Flipkart and Shopee
competitors.funding_then: Series C of about A$100M (US$50M per one outlet) in September 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: API and rating engine on top of insurer partners with compliance logic; the hard part was licensing and insurer relationships more than software.

defensibility.rationale: Insurance licensing, carrier relationships and deep platform integrations are slower to copy than the API itself.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or incumbent copy found through early 2022; the company raised a $25M Series A in February 2022.

market_need_then: Rental and gig platforms such as Outdoorsy already sold insurance with transactions and lacked in house underwriting and compliance; the founders saw this at Turo.

branding.community_and_virality: No brand specific community or merch found; the name is shared with unrelated companies such as a marketing platform called Tint.

brand_strength.rationale: Short, easy name but shared with unrelated companies, with press focused on funding rather than the brand.

outcome_analysis: Two ex Turo operators built embedded insurance infrastructure, raised a $3.75M seed in March 2021 and a $25M Series A led by QED in February 2022, with total capital of $30M. Founder market fit and the embedded finance wave helped. The directory lists a 40 person team and Active status, and no later round, acquisition or layoff was found.
notes: Series A stated by many outlets; Crowdfund Insider calls it a Series B, treated as an outlier. BounceWatch dates the seed 2021-04-10; press says March 2021. Seed investors are not separately named in the press release (it names existing investors Nyca, Deciens, YC and Webb), so the seed investor list is empty. The Business Wire page returned HTTP 403 when fetched, so Series A details come from its search snippet and The Insurer. Cover Genius is dated six months after the batch and noted as such; the company existed before the batch. tint.ai was not fetched. Medium retrospective on the Series A journey was not opened.
